description: Base 9: build on Base 8 (voice-1f4d3de1, v308_generalist_handle_gear). Jake: Add a piece on top so everything stays centered: a top plate similar to the bottom base piece, so the geared handle pieces are captured and supported from both sides (above and below), and their axles are held at both ends so they stay aligned. Keep it printable without supports, and keep the motor underneath.

results.identified_issue: Gripper 21's J-hook covers the pivot (probe: the finger intersects even an r=2 cylinder at the pivot), so a through-axle would need a hole in the finger, which is a Gripper change. I chose a C-shaped rib (top plate) in a C-shaped groove (handle-gear hub top). The groove is the annulus at ring_r minus offset(ring_wall) of profile(). The rib is the narrower annulus intersected with rotate(-a) of the groove sector for a in 0..30 (intersection_for), so it fits at every swing. Top plate outline: top_bush_r 11.5 < bush_r. Wider plate corners, or a hull out to the upper pillar, enter the lower strap slot's strap_zone (strap_tunnel check). So the upper pillar hangs on a separate hull strip. ring_r went 10 -> 9.5 so the rib stays 0.45 mm or more inside the plate edge (it poked 0.05 past at 10 and failed the overhang check). Alternatives if Jake wants a true full axle: Gripper 22 with a pivot hole through the hook plus a steel pin from base to top plate. Unverified: prints, M3 self-tap pull-out, rib wear/wobble.
results.summary: Base 9: a top plate over the handle-gears, fingers and pinion. Each handle-gear now turns on the base's post below and on a C-shaped ring under the plate above, so both ends of its axis are held. All 50 geometry checks pass, including no supports needed.
results.detailed_description:
Base 9 is Base 8 with a seventh printed part, the top plate (v309_generalist_top_plate). It's a flat 4 mm plate shaped like the base (the outline round both pivots and the pinion), 0.3 mm above everything that turns. It stands on three pillars: two below the pinion and one on the centreline above where the gears mesh. Each pillar's foot drops into a 1.5 mm socket in the base, which lines the plate up with the posts. Three M3 countersunk screws come up through the base into the pillars. The base got bigger to reach the pillars, and the motor is still underneath, unchanged.

One thing works differently from what you might picture. The finger's base hook sits right over the pivot, so the post can't run up through to the plate. Instead each handle-gear's hub has a C-shaped groove round its pivot, cut down from the top face wherever the finger isn't. A matching C-shaped ring under the plate runs in that groove. The ring is about 250° of a circle, open where the finger is, and shortened so it never hits the groove's ends over the 0–30° swing. The base post holds the bottom of each axis and the ring holds the top. With the plate on, neither a handle-gear nor a finger can lift out (Base 8 relied on gravity).

The plate also has a hole over the pinion, so its 3 screws can still be reached with the plate on. The plate prints top face down, with the rings and pillars standing straight up. The new screw holes in the base are countersunk from underneath at 45°. One trade-off: the plate's disc round each pivot is 11.5 mm (the base's is 11). Any wider and its corners would run into the space the strap needs at the lower strap slot. The upper pillar joins the plate along a strip down the centreline for the same reason. Every size is a new param in the Tune panel's 'Top plate (Base 9)' group (17 of them).

Piece count goes from 13 to 17: 7 printed parts, the RS00 and 9 M3 screws. The checks prove nothing that turns touches the plate at any angle from 0 to 30°. Lifting a handle-gear or finger 0.5 mm makes it hit the plate, and shifting a handle-gear 0.5 mm sideways makes it hit its ring. The strap-slot clearances still hold and the plate needs no supports. Nothing has been sliced or printed. The ring is a printed C, not a full bearing, and the screws cut their own threads in printed pillars, which hasn't been pull-tested.

summary: Base 9 needs a top plate, like the bottom base piece, above the geared handle pieces from Base 8. It should hold their axles at both ends for alignment, stay printable without supports, and keep the motor underneath.
